_readme: A theme picks which rooms a run can use and which shapes those rooms can take.
Add a theme here, then set "theme" on an entry in sizes.json or levels.json.
Room ids must exist in rooms.json.
Shapes: "rect" (default), "round", "hex" — all three are implemented in
css/room.css and in inShape() in js/geometry.js. This list is the pool a room
draws from; a room in rooms.json can pin its own "shape" and ignore it.
A theme may list far more rooms than a house has cells (the grid holds 9).
That surplus IS the variety: each run draws a different subset.
Every key under "themes" is a theme — do not park notes in there.
AN EMOJI'S HOME IS UNIQUE PER THEME, NOT GLOBALLY. A run only ever draws
rooms from one theme, so two themes may each give the same emoji a home;
within one theme two homes still makes a run unwinnable and is an error.
That is what lets `dream` use 🪐 🔭 🌙 🛰️ while the house Observatory
keeps them too. See check 1 in js/validate.js.
DREAM: the tidier is working so hard they dream about tidying. The frame
is a wrapper rather than one setting — it can hold any world without
explaining how the player got there, and space is only the first.
